hero.titleLine2: to Claude, Cursor, any MCP client
hero.lead: Give your AI agent a real Telekom inbox. Read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize mail over IMAP using the dedicated password Telekom issues for mail programs.
hero.answer: Claude cannot reach a T-Online mailbox on its own. mcpemails is a hosted MCP server that connects it over IMAP at secureimap.t-online.de on port 993, authenticating with the separate Passwort für E-Mail-Programme that Telekom issues for mail clients rather than your Telekom login password, so Claude, Cursor or any MCP client can read, search, send and organize the mail. If you have never created that password, no client has ever been able to log in to the mailbox and the failure looks like a typo. One inbox is free, forever.

method.title: How T-Online connects: IMAP and a second, separate password
method.body: Telekom documents the same servers for every @t-online.de and @magenta.de address: IMAP at secureimap.t-online.de on port 993 with SSL, and SMTP at securesmtp.t-online.de on port 465 or 587. Both names sit in front of an IMAP proxy rather than a mailbox server you talk to directly, which explains several of the quirks below. The part almost everyone gets wrong is the credential. Telekom keeps two passwords on one account: the Telekom Login password, used for the E-Mail Center, the Kundencenter and the MeinMagenta app, and a second Passwort für E-Mail-Programme, which Telekom says you need as soon as you read your mail in a program such as Outlook or Thunderbird instead of the E-Mail Center. Only the second one authenticates against secureimap.t-online.de, and Telekom advises that the two be different.

setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com. The free plan connects one inbox forever and does not ask for a card.

In the E-Mail Center at email.t-online.de, click the gear icon (Einstellungen), then Alle Einstellungen anzeigen, then Passwörter, then Passwort für E-Mail-Programme, and set a new one. The other route is the Kundencenter: Profil verwalten, then Login-Daten, then Weitere Passwörter. Telekom advises making it different from your Telekom Login password.
Choose IMAP / SMTP, enter the full address such as name@t-online.de, and paste the mail-program password. The Telekom hosts and ports are prefilled and were verified from a live TLS connection.

setup.h: Paste the MCP URL into your AI
setup.p: Drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT, authorize, and your agent has the inbox.

gotchas.h: The Telekom login password is rejected, and that is by design
gotchas.p: This is the single most common T-Online connection failure and it produces an ordinary authentication error with nothing in it to tell you why. Telekom splits the account into a login password for telekom.de and the Kundencenter, and a separate Passwort für E-Mail-Programme for IMAP, POP3 and SMTP. The mail server accepts only the second one. Telekom explicitly advises that the two should differ, so even setting them to the same string is not the intended fix; create the mail-program password, then use it in both the incoming and the outgoing side of the connection.

gotchas.h: The IMAP proxy advertises no AUTH mechanism at all before login
gotchas.p: The capability banner Telekom returns is IMAP4 IMAP4rev1 QUOTA LITERAL+ NAMESPACE UIDPLUS IDLE SORT. There is no AUTH=PLAIN, no AUTH=LOGIN and no SASL-IR in it. In practice the server expects the plain IMAP LOGIN command rather than a SASL AUTHENTICATE exchange. Client libraries that enumerate advertised SASL mechanisms and refuse to proceed when the list is empty give up before they ever send credentials, which is why some IMAP tooling reports T-Online as unreachable while Thunderbird connects to the same mailbox without complaint. mcpemails handles the bare LOGIN path, so this one is already dealt with for you.

gotchas.h: No MOVE and no SPECIAL-USE, on a mailbox with German folder names
gotchas.p: The server does not advertise the IMAP MOVE extension, so filing a message is performed as a copy, a flag update and an expunge rather than one atomic command. It also omits SPECIAL-USE, which means Sent, Drafts, Trash and Junk are identified by name and not by role. A T-Online mailbox normally names them Gesendet, Entwürfe, Papierkorb and Spam, so if an agent cannot find your archive or sent folder, name it in the instruction.

gotchas.h: Sending is capped at 50 MB per message
gotchas.p: securesmtp.t-online.de announces a maximum message size of 52,428,800 bytes. That is the size of the whole encoded message, so base64 attachments count roughly a third larger than their size on disk. An agent asked to forward a large attachment will get a hard SMTP rejection rather than a slow send.

gotchas.h: Telekom can hold a send from an internet connection it does not know
gotchas.p: Telekom checks the internet connection a message is sent from. Its help says that when a mail program sends from an unknown or unapproved IP address, the message is not sent and the program gets an error, and it names another Wi-Fi network, a mobile network, a VPN or a connection abroad as common causes. Mail your agent sends through MCP Emails leaves from MCP Emails' servers, not from your home connection, so it can be held the same way. Telekom says you can approve (freischalten) the IP address if the attempt was yours. If it was not, do not approve it, and change your Telekom Login password.

limits: Because the server has no MOVE support, a move is not atomic. If a connection drops mid-operation a message can briefly exist in both folders.

Telekom scopes the mail-program password to mail clients. It does not unlock the Kundencenter, and rotating your Telekom login password does not rotate it, so the two have to be maintained separately.

faq.q: Does Claude work with T-Online email?
faq.a: Not on its own. Claude has no built-in Telekom or T-Online connector. Pointing an MCP server such as mcpemails at the mailbox over IMAP gives Claude read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize access to it, and the same connection then works from Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP clients.

faq.q: What are the T-Online IMAP and SMTP settings?
faq.a: IMAP is secureimap.t-online.de on port 993 with SSL. SMTP is securesmtp.t-online.de on port 465 or 587, also with SSL; MCP Emails uses 465. Log in with your full address and the Passwort für E-Mail-Programme. Telekom lists the same servers for @t-online.de and @magenta.de addresses, and both hosts were confirmed from a live TLS connection.

faq.q: Why is my T-Online password rejected in an email program?
faq.a: Almost always because you entered the Telekom Login password. Telekom issues a second credential, the Passwort für E-Mail-Programme, and only that one authenticates against the mail servers. Create or reset it in the E-Mail Center under the gear icon, Alle Einstellungen anzeigen, Passwörter, or in the Kundencenter under Profil verwalten, Login-Daten, Weitere Passwörter.

faq.q: Where do I create the Passwort für E-Mail-Programme?
faq.a: There are two places. In the E-Mail Center at email.t-online.de, click the gear icon (Einstellungen), then Alle Einstellungen anzeigen, then Passwörter, then Passwort für E-Mail-Programme. In the Kundencenter, open Profil verwalten, then Login-Daten, then Weitere Passwörter. Use the new value in MCP Emails, for both the incoming and the outgoing server.

faq.q: Does this work with magenta.de addresses?
faq.a: Yes. Telekom documents the same servers for @magenta.de and @t-online.de addresses: secureimap.t-online.de for IMAP and securesmtp.t-online.de for SMTP, with the Passwort für E-Mail-Programme as the password and the full address as the username.

faq.q: Is my T-Online mail stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Messages are fetched live from Telekom over IMAP for each request and handed to your AI client. Credentials are encrypted at rest and message bodies are not retained.
